subject: Observability add-ons — retention surge credits, tracing seats, and dashboard SKUs
messages:
--- Message 1 ---
From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: jamie.ortiz@blueharborpharma.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Observability add-ons — quick packaging options for retention/tracing

Jamie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, I pulled together three pragmatic packaging options for observability (retention tiers, tracing egress, advanced dashboards) so your infra and product teams can model cost vs signal fidelity. Attached is a short SKU grid and an example monthly burn for your current footprint.

High-level options:
- Option A: Base visibility (30d retention, 10M trace spans/mo) — lowest cost, minimal dashboards
- Option B: Standard (90d retention, 50M spans/mo, 3 advanced dashboards) — recommended for clinical analytics pilots
- Option C: Premium (365d retention, 200M spans/mo, unlimited dashboards + priority support) — for full platform rollout

Two open asks from your side: 1) if you prefer slab pricing or metered usage for traces, and 2) whether seats for dashboard editors should be per-user or per-team. If you send back a target ARR or committed monthly spend, I can model a concession path.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0183

Attachment: Observability_SKU_quote_20261201.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

--- Message 2 ---
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@blueharborpharma.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — quick packaging options for retention/tracing

Soojin —

Thanks for the breakdown. Quick answers:
1) Procurement prefers slab pricing with clear overage bands we can forecast. Metered is fine for pilot but procurement will push to a capped slab for Q1.
2) Dashboard seats: we want 5 editor seats initially and an unlimited viewer role.

We are targeting an ARR band of $120k-$160k for base infra + add-ons for the first year. If we can get a predictable slab for traces and a credit path for retention surges (we expect seasonal spikes around batch runs), that will help us get internal approval.

Can you share a proposal that maps that ARR range to Option B with a capped trace slab and a surge-credit mechanism?

— Jamie
Head of Platform
BlueHarbor Pharma

--- Message 3 (internal) ---
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Observability add-ons — strategy for BlueHarbor concession

Looping Markus for pricing/product confirmation. Notes:
- Target ARR 120-160k; likely want Option B as base.
- Procurement wants slab + capped overage; also surge credits for retention windows.
- They asked for 5 editor seats + unlimited viewers (viewer free).

Markus — can we:
1) present a 12-month slab for traces at 50M spans/mo with a 20% overage band priced at a premium?
2) include a one-time pool of "retention surge credits" (e.g., 200GB-month) that they can apply for Q1 batch runs?
3) provide a 15% committed discount at $140k ARR and 20% at $160k ARR?

I think concessions are reasonable but need product sign-off on surge credits (how we bill and cap).

— Vanessa (AE Manager)

--- Message 4 (internal reply) ---
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Observability add-ons — strategy for BlueHarbor concession

We can do the slab + overage structure. Proposed terms:
- Tracing: 50M spans/month slab, 20% overage at 2.5x unit price. Overage triggers a courtesy notification and temporary throttling threshold unless they approve auto-billing.
- Retention surge credits: one-time pool (200 GB-month) applied to raw storage for 3 months. Credits are non-recurring; additional surge will be billed per GB at standard rate.
- Dashboard seats: 5 editors at seat price, viewers unlimited (view-only token).
- Discount bands: 15% at $140k ARR commit; 22% at $170k ARR commit.

I recommend we offer 18% at $155k as a middle ground (sales can position as limited-time). Product OK with non-recurring credits if they are tracked via the console and can be clawed back if abused.

— Markus (Head of Product Pricing)

--- Message 5 ---
From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: jamie.ortiz@blueharborpharma.com, procurement@blueharborpharma.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposal: Option B (standard) with slab + surge-credit concession (RDW-3773)

Jamie / Procurement —

Attached is a concise proposal and draft SLA addendum that reflects your asks. Key changes from the original SKU grid: 
- Tracing slab: 50M spans / month; 20% overage band at 2.5x; courtesy notifications and optional auto-billing for overage.
- Retention: 90d base retention; one-time retention surge credit pool of 200 GB-month usable over Q1 2027. Credits are non-recurring and tracked in the console.
- Dashboards: 5 editor seats (paid), unlimited view-only seats.
- Pricing: modeled two commit tiers: $140k ARR = 15% discount; $160k ARR = 20% discount. We included an intermediate commercial offer shown at $155k with 18% discount (limited-time).

Attachments: Observability_SKU_quote_20261214.pdf (proposal with numbers) and SLA_Addendum_BlueHarbor_v1.docx (legal redline).

Next steps: if $155k is acceptable we can cut a DPA + SOW and move to procurement. If procurement needs a different cadence, let's schedule a short call this week.

Thanks —

— Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

--- Message 6 ---
From: Procurement <procurement@blueharborpharma.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: jamie.ortiz@blueharborpharma.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Option B (standard) with slab + surge-credit concession (RDW-3773)

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Procurement appreciates the slab + surge-credit approach. Two clarifying questions before we route to finance: 
1) Can the 200 GB-month surge credit be converted to a refundable credit (applied to a future month) if unused? We prefer credits that offset invoiced usage rather than one-time write-offs.
2) For the tracing overage pricing, will you accept a 2.0x multiplier for the first 10% overage band (instead of 2.5x) and then 3.0x thereafter? This helps us forecast worst-case spend.

If you can accept those two edits, procurement will prepare the contract redlines and target signature in mid-January. Please respond with final line items and updated PDF.

— Procurement Team
BlueHarbor Pharma
